topics: Circle geometry, arc lengths & sector areas

body.en: Geometry represents approximately 10% of the EST I Mathematics exam. Candidates must master Euclidean and coordinate geometry: parallel lines with transversals, polygon angle properties, special right triangles (\(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) and \(30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ\)), circle equations in standard and general forms, inscribed angle relationships, arc lengths and sector areas, and 3D volumetric scaling.
body.ar: الهندسة represents approximately 10% of the EST I Mathematics exam. Candidates must master Euclidean and الإحداثي الهندسة: parallel lines with transversals, polygon الزاوية properties, special right triangles (\(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) and \(30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ\)), الدائرة المعادلات in standard and general forms, inscribed الزاوية relationships, arc lengths and sector areas, and 3D volumetric scaling.

label.en: Definition 6.1 — Angles, Polygons, Similarity, and Circle Relationships
label.ar: تعريف 6.1 — Angles, Polygons, Similarity, and الدائرة Relationships

body.en:
Foundational geometric properties and theorems:
  • Lines, Transversals, and Angles:
    Parallel lines cut by a transversal produce equal alternate interior, alternate exterior, and corresponding angles; consecutive interior angles are supplementary (sum to \(180^\circ\)).
  • Polygon Angle Formulas:
    For any convex polygon with \(n\) sides:
    1. Sum of Interior Angles: \(S_{\text{int}} = (n - 2) \times 180^\circ\).
    2. Each Interior Angle (Regular \(n\)-gon): \(\theta_{\text{int}} = \frac{(n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{n}\).
    3. Sum of Exterior Angles: \(S_{\text{ext}} = 360^\circ\) for all convex polygons.
  • Similarity and Scaling Laws:
    If two figures or solids are geometrically similar with linear scale factor \(k = \frac{L_2}{L_1}\):
    1. Perimeter ratio: \(\frac{P_2}{P_1} = k\).
    2. Surface area ratio: \(\frac{A_2}{A_1} = k^2\).
    3. Volume ratio: \(\frac{V_2}{V_1} = k^3\).
  • Circle Geometry & Inscribed Angles:
    1. Central vs. Inscribed Angle: An inscribed angle \(\angle ACB\) intercepting arc \(AB\) is exactly half the measure of the central angle \(\angle AOB\):
    \[ \angle ACB = \frac{1}{2} \angle AOB \]
    2. Thales's Theorem: An angle inscribed in a semicircle (subtending a diameter) is always a right angle (\(90^\circ\)).
    3. Arc Length & Sector Area (central angle \(\theta\) in degrees):
    \[ s = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ}(2\pi r), \qquad A_{\text{sector}} = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ}(\pi r^2) \]
body.ar:
Foundational geometric properties and theorems:
  • Lines, Transversals, and Angles:

    2. Each Interior الزاوية (Regular \(n\)-gon): \(\theta_{\text{int}} = \frac{(n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{n}\).
    3. Sum of Exterior Angles: \(S_{\text{ext}} = 360^\circ\) for all convex polygons.
  • Similarity and Scaling Laws:

    2. Surface المساحة ratio: \(\frac{A_2}{A_1} = k^2\).
    3. الحجم ratio: \(\frac{V_2}{V_1} = k^3\).
  • Circle الهندسة & Inscribed Angles:
    1. Central vs. Inscribed الزاوية: An inscribed الزاوية \(\angle ACB\) intercepting arc \(AB\) is exactly half the measure of the central الزاوية \(\angle AOB\):
    \[ \angle ACB = \frac{1}{2} \angle AOB \]
    2. Thales's مبرهنة: An الزاوية inscribed in a semicircle (subtending a القطر) is always a right الزاوية (\(90^\circ\)).
    3. Arc Length & Sector المساحة (central الزاوية \(\theta\) in degrees):
    \[ s = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ}(2\pi r), \qquad A_{\text{sector}} = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ}(\pi r^2) \]

body.en: Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).
body.ar: Euclidean Invariants, Locus المعادلات & Scaling Laws: In analytic الهندسة, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A الدائرة of center \((h, k)\) and نصف القطر \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a خط المماس at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the نصف القطر \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

label.en: Theorem 6.1 — Right Triangle Ratios, Coordinate Circles, and 3D Solid Mensuration
label.ar: مبرهنة 6.1 — Right المثلث Ratios, الإحداثي Circles, and 3D Solid Mensuration

body.en:
Key spatial relationships and analytical formulas tested on EST I:
  • Special Right Triangles:
    • \(45^\circ-45^\circ-90^\circ\) (Isosceles Right): Sides are in ratio \(1 : 1 : \sqrt{2}\). Hypotenuse is \(\text{leg} \times \sqrt{2}\).
    • \(30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ\): Sides are in ratio \(1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\). Side opposite \(30^\circ\) is \(x\), side opposite \(60^\circ\) is \(x\sqrt{3}\), and hypotenuse is \(2x\).
  • Circle Equations in the Coordinate Plane:
    Standard form with center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\):
    \[ (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 \]
    To transform the general equation \(x^2 + y^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\) into standard form, complete the square independently for \(x\) and \(y\).
  • 3D Mensuration Formulas:
    • Right Circular Cylinder: Volume \(V = \pi r^2 h\), Lateral Area \(= 2\pi rh\), Total Area \(= 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2\).
    • Right Circular Cone: Volume \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\).
    • Sphere: Volume \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), Surface Area \(A = 4\pi r^2\).
    • Right Pyramid: Volume \(V = \frac{1}{3} B h\), where \(B\) is base area.

  • Circle المعادلات in the الإحداثي Plane:

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Geometry & Measurement
label.ar: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — الهندسة & Measurement

body.en:
• Area vs. Circumference Formulas: Circle area is \(A = \pi r^2\); circumference is \(C = 2\pi r\). If a question provides the diameter, divide by 2 to get the radius \(r = d/2\) before squaring! Squaring the diameter is the most common geometry blunder on EST I.
  • Inscribed vs. Central Angles: An inscribed angle with vertex on the circle circumference measures exactly HALF the central angle intercepting the same arc: \(\angle_{\text{inscribed}} = \frac{1}{2}\angle_{\text{central}}\). Any inscribed angle intercepting a diameter measures \(90^\circ\).
  • Similar Solids Scaling: If the ratio of linear lengths between two similar figures is \(k\), their surface areas scale as \(k^2\), and their volumes scale as \(k^3\). Never use the linear scale factor to scale volume directly.
  • Circle Equation Center Signs: In \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\), the center is \((h, k)\). For \((x + 4)^2 + (y - 7)^2 = 36\), the center is \((-4, 7)\) and radius is \(\sqrt{36} = 6\), NOT 36!
body.ar:
• Area vs. Circumference الصيغ: الدائرة المساحة is \(A = \pi r^2\); circumference is \(C = 2\pi r\). If a question provides the القطر, divide by 2 to get the نصف القطر \(r = d/2\) before squaring! Squaring the القطر is the most common الهندسة blunder on EST I.
  • Inscribed vs. Central Angles: An inscribed الزاوية with الرأس on the الدائرة circumference measures exactly HALF the central الزاوية intercepting the same arc: \(\angle_{\text{inscribed}} = \frac{1}{2}\angle_{\text{central}}\). Any inscribed الزاوية intercepting a القطر measures \(90^\circ\).
  • Similar Solids Scaling: If the ratio of linear lengths between two similar figures is \(k\), their surface areas scale as \(k^2\), and their volumes scale as \(k^3\). Never use the linear scale factor to scale الحجم directly.
  • Circle المعادلة Center Signs: In \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\), the center is \((h, k)\). For \((x + 4)^2 + (y - 7)^2 = 36\), the center is \((-4, 7)\) and نصف القطر is \(\sqrt{36} = 6\), NOT 36!

label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (الهندسة)

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).
body.ar:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central الزاوية & الدائرة Completion Works: المعطيات \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the نصف القطر is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any الدائرة, drawing القطر \(POQ\) splits an inscribed الزاوية \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior الزاوية المبرهنة, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

label.en: Worked Example 6.A — Circle Equation by Completing the Square
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.A — الدائرة المعادلة by Completing the Square

body.en:
The equation of a circle in the \(xy\)-plane is given by \(x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y - 11 = 0\).
(a) Find the coordinates of the center \((h, k)\) and the radius \(r\).
(b) Determine the exact area of the circle in terms of \(\pi\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Complete the square:
    Group \(x\) and \(y\) terms, moving constant 11 to the right side:
    \[ (x^2 - 8x) + (y^2 + 6y) = 11 \]
    Complete the square for \(x\): half of \(-8\) is \(-4\), and \((-4)^2 = 16\).
    Complete the square for \(y\): half of \(+6\) is \(+3\), and \((+3)^2 = 9\).
    Add 16 and 9 to BOTH sides:
    \[ (x^2 - 8x + 16) + (y^2 + 6y + 9) = 11 + 16 + 9 \implies (x - 4)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 36 \]
  2. Extract center and radius:
    Center: \(\mathbf{(4, -3)}\)
    Radius: \(r = \sqrt{36} = \mathbf{6}\)
  3. (b) Calculate Area:
    \[ A = \pi r^2 = \pi (6^2) = \mathbf{36\pi} \]
body.ar:
The المعادلة of a الدائرة in the \(xy\)-plane is المعطيات by \(x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y - 11 = 0\).
(a) أوجد إحداثيات the center \((h, k)\) and the نصف القطر \(r\).
(b) حدّد exact المساحة of the الدائرة in terms of \(\pi\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Complete the square:
    Group \(x\) and \(y\) terms, moving الثابت 11 to the right side:
    \[ (x^2 - 8x) + (y^2 + 6y) = 11 \]
    Complete the square for \(x\): half of \(-8\) is \(-4\), and \((-4)^2 = 16\).
    Complete the square for \(y\): half of \(+6\) is \(+3\), and \((+3)^2 = 9\).
    Add 16 and 9 to BOTH sides:
    \[ (x^2 - 8x + 16) + (y^2 + 6y + 9) = 11 + 16 + 9 \implies (x - 4)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 36 \]
  2. Extract center and نصف القطر:
    Center: \(\mathbf{(4, -3)}\)
    Radius: \(r = \sqrt{36} = \mathbf{6}\)
  3. (b) احسب المساحة:
    \[ A = \pi r^2 = \pi (6^2) = \mathbf{36\pi} \]

label.en: Worked Example 6.B — Inscribed Angles, Central Angles & Sector Shading
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.B — Inscribed Angles, Central Angles & Sector Shading

body.en:
A circle with center \(O\) has a radius of \(12\text{ cm}\). Points \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) lie on the circumference such that inscribed angle \(\angle ACB = 45^\circ\).
(a) Determine the measure of central angle \(\angle AOB\).
(b) Calculate the exact length of minor arc \(AB\).
(c) Calculate the exact area of sector \(AOB\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Central Angle Measure:
    By the Inscribed Angle Theorem, the central angle is twice the inscribed angle intercepting the same arc:
    \[ \angle AOB = 2 \times \angle ACB = 2 \times 45^\circ = \mathbf{90^\circ} \]
  2. (b) Arc Length Calculation:
    The arc length represents \(\frac{90^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{1}{4}\) of the full circumference:
    \[ s = \frac{90^\circ}{360^\circ} \times (2\pi r) = \frac{1}{4} \times 2\pi(12) = \frac{24\pi}{4} = \mathbf{6\pi\text{ cm}} \]
  3. (c) Sector Area Calculation:
    \[ A_{\text{sector}} = \frac{90^\circ}{360^\circ} \times (\pi r^2) = \frac{1}{4} \times \pi(12^2) = \frac{144\pi}{4} = \mathbf{36\pi\text{ cm}^2} \]
body.ar:
A الدائرة with center \(O\) has a نصف القطر of \(12\text{ cm}\). Points \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) lie on the circumference such that inscribed الزاوية \(\angle ACB = 45^\circ\).
(a) حدّد measure of central الزاوية \(\angle AOB\).
(b) احسب exact length of minor arc \(AB\).
(c) احسب exact المساحة of sector \(AOB\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Central الزاوية Measure:
    By the Inscribed الزاوية مبرهنة, the central الزاوية is twice the inscribed الزاوية intercepting the same arc:
    \[ \angle AOB = 2 \times \angle ACB = 2 \times 45^\circ = \mathbf{90^\circ} \]
  2. (b) Arc Length Calculation:
    The arc length represents \(\frac{90^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{1}{4}\) of the full circumference:
    \[ s = \frac{90^\circ}{360^\circ} \times (2\pi r) = \frac{1}{4} \times 2\pi(12) = \frac{24\pi}{4} = \mathbf{6\pi\text{ cm}} \]
  3. (c) Sector المساحة Calculation:
    \[ A_{\text{sector}} = \frac{90^\circ}{360^\circ} \times (\pi r^2) = \frac{1}{4} \times \pi(12^2) = \frac{144\pi}{4} = \mathbf{36\pi\text{ cm}^2} \]

label.en: Worked Example 6.C — Similar Solids Scaling & Volume Optimization
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.C — Similar Solids Scaling & الحجم Optimization

body.en:
Two geometrically similar right cones have base radii of 6 cm and 9 cm, respectively.
(a) What is the ratio of their total surface areas?
(b) If the smaller cone has a volume of \(160\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is the exact volume of the larger cone?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Surface Area Ratio:
    Find the linear scale factor \(k\):
    \[ k = \frac{r_2}{r_1} = \frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5 \]
    Surface areas scale with the square of the linear ratio:
    \[ \frac{A_2}{A_1} = k^2 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \mathbf{\frac{9}{4} = 2.25} \]
  2. (b) Volume of Larger Cone:
    Volumes scale with the cube of the linear ratio:
    \[ \frac{V_2}{V_1} = k^3 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8} \]
    Multiply the smaller volume by \(\frac{27}{8}\):
    \[ V_2 = 160\pi \times \frac{27}{8} = 20\pi \times 27 = \mathbf{540\pi\text{ cm}^3} \]
body.ar:
Two geometrically similar right cones have base radii of 6 cm and 9 cm, respectively.
(a) What is the ratio of their total surface areas?
(b) If the smaller cone has a الحجم of \(160\pi\text{ cm}^3\), what is the exact الحجم of the larger cone?

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Surface المساحة Ratio:
    Find the linear scale factor \(k\):
    \[ k = \frac{r_2}{r_1} = \frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5 \]
    Surface areas scale with the square of the linear ratio:
    \[ \frac{A_2}{A_1} = k^2 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \mathbf{\frac{9}{4} = 2.25} \]
  2. (b) الحجم of Larger Cone:
    Volumes scale with the cube of the linear ratio:
    \[ \frac{V_2}{V_1} = k^3 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8} \]
    Multiply the smaller الحجم by \(\frac{27}{8}\):
    \[ V_2 = 160\pi \times \frac{27}{8} = 20\pi \times 27 = \mathbf{540\pi\text{ cm}^3} \]

body.en:
Problem (Medium): In the diagram below, line segment \( DE \) is parallel to line segment \( BC \). If \( AD = 6 \), \( DB = 4 \), and \( AE = 9 \), what is the length of \( EC \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Since \( DE \) is parallel to \( BC \), by the Triangle Proportionality Theorem (also known as Thales's Theorem or the Basic Proportionality Theorem), the line \( DE \) divides the sides \( AB \) and \( AC \) proportionally. This means that the ratio of \( AD \) to \( DB \) is equal to the ratio of \( AE \) to \( EC \). \[ \frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{AE}{EC} \] We are given the lengths: \( AD = 6 \), \( DB = 4 \), and \( AE = 9 \). We need to find \( EC \). Substitute the given values into the equation: \[ \frac{6}{4} = \frac{9}{EC} \] To solve for \( EC \), we can cross-multiply: \[ 6 \times EC = 4 \times 9 \] \[ 6 EC = 36 \] Now, divide by 6: \[ EC = \frac{36}{6} \] \[ EC = 6 \] Therefore, the length of \( EC \) is 6.
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): In the المخطط below, line segment \( DE \) is parallel to line segment \( BC \). If \( AD = 6 \), \( DB = 4 \), and \( AE = 9 \), what is the length of \( EC \)?

Step-by-Step الحل: Since \( DE \) is parallel to \( BC \), by the المثلث Proportionality مبرهنة (also known as Thales's مبرهنة or the Basic Proportionality مبرهنة), the line \( DE \) divides the sides \( AB \) and \( AC \) proportionally. This means that the ratio of \( AD \) to \( DB \) is equal to the ratio of \( AE \) to \( EC \). \[ \frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{AE}{EC} \] We are المعطيات the lengths: \( AD = 6 \), \( DB = 4 \), and \( AE = 9 \). We need to find \( EC \). عوّض the المعطيات values into the المعادلة: \[ \frac{6}{4} = \frac{9}{EC} \] To أوجد قيمة \( EC \), we can cross-multiply: \[ 6 \times EC = 4 \times 9 \] \[ 6 EC = 36 \] Now, divide by 6: \[ EC = \frac{36}{6} \] \[ EC = 6 \] وبالتالي, the length of \( EC \) is 6.

question.en: A line segment connects points \(P(-3, 7)\) and \(Q(5, -1)\). Determine: (a) the exact length of \(PQ\), (b) the coordinates of the midpoint \(M\), and (c) the slope of the perpendicular bisector of \(PQ\).
question.ar: A line segment connects points \(P(-3, 7)\) and \(Q(5, -1)\). حدّد: (a) the exact length of \(PQ\), (b) the coordinates of the midpoint \(M\), and (c) the slope of the perpendicular bisector of \(PQ\).

solution.en:
(a) Distance formula: \[ PQ = \sqrt{(5 - (-3))^2 + (-1 - 7)^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + (-8)^2} = \sqrt{64 + 64} = \sqrt{128} = \mathbf{8\sqrt{2}}. \]

(b) Midpoint formula: \[ M = \left(\frac{-3 + 5}{2}, \frac{7 + (-1)}{2}\right) = \left(\frac{2}{2}, \frac{6}{2}\right) = \mathbf{(1, 3)}. \]

(c) Perpendicular slope: Slope of \(PQ\) is \(m = \frac{-1 - 7}{5 - (-3)} = \frac{-8}{8} = -1\). The perpendicular bisector has negative reciprocal slope: \[ m_\perp = -\frac{1}{-1} = \mathbf{+1}. \]

question.en: An equilateral triangle has a side length of \(12\text{ cm}\). Find: (a) the exact length of its altitude, and (b) its exact area.
question.ar: An equilateral triangle has a side length of \(12\text{ cm}\). أوجد: (a) the exact length of its altitude, and (b) its exact area.

solution.en:
(a) Altitude using \(30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ\) triangle: Dropping an altitude splits the equilateral triangle into two congruent \(30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ\) right triangles with short leg \(b/2 = 6\text{ cm}\) and hypotenuse \(12\text{ cm}\). The altitude is opposite the \(60^\circ\) angle: \[ h = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}. \]

(b) Area formula: \[ A = \frac{1}{2} b h = \frac{1}{2}(12)(6\sqrt{3}) = \mathbf{36\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2}. \] (Alternatively: \(A = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} s^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(144) = 36\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2\)).

question.en: Determine the equation of the circle in the \(xy\)-plane for which the segment connecting \(A(2, -3)\) and \(B(8, 5)\) serves as a diameter.
question.ar: حدّد equation of the circle in the \(xy\)-plane for which the segment connecting \(A(2, -3)\) and \(B(8, 5)\) serves as a diameter.

solution.en:
Step 1: The center \((h, k)\) is the midpoint of diameter \(AB\): \[ (h, k) = \left(\frac{2 + 8}{2}, \frac{-3 + 5}{2}\right) = \left(\frac{10}{2}, \frac{2}{2}\right) = \mathbf{(5, 1)}. \]

Step 2: Compute radius \(r\) as the distance from center \((5, 1)\) to \(B(8, 5)\): \[ r^2 = (8 - 5)^2 + (5 - 1)^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 \implies r = 5. \]

Step 3: Write standard equation: \[ \mathbf{(x - 5)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 25}. \]

question.en: A solid metal cone with base radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and height \(9\text{ cm}\) is submerged into a cylindrical beaker with internal radius \(6\text{ cm}\) partially filled with water. Assuming the cone is fully submerged and no water overflows, by how many centimeters does the water level in the beaker rise?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Geometry): A solid metal cone with base radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and height \(9\text{ cm}\) is submerged into a cylindrical beaker with internal radius \(6\text{ cm}\) partially filled with water. Assuming the cone is fully submerged and no water overflows, by how many centimeters does the water level in the beaker rise?

solution.en:
Step 1: Compute the volume of the submerged cone: \[ V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3} \pi r_{\text{cone}}^2 h_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3} \pi (4^2)(9) = \frac{1}{3} \pi (16)(9) = 48\pi\text{ cm}^3. \]

Step 2: The volume of water displaced forms a cylinder with radius \(R = 6\text{ cm}\) and height \(\Delta h\): \[ V_{\text{displaced}} = \pi R^2 (\Delta h) = \pi (6^2) \Delta h = 36\pi \Delta h. \]

Step 3: Equate volumes and solve for \(\Delta h\): \[ 36\pi \Delta h = 48\pi \implies \Delta h = \frac{48\pi}{36\pi} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.33\text{ cm}. \]

The water level rises by exactly \(\mathbf{\frac{4}{3}\text{ cm}}\) (or \(\mathbf{1.33\text{ cm}}\)).

question.en: In the given diagram, \(\triangle ABC\) is inscribed in a circle. Points \(D\) and \(E\) lie on sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) respectively. It is given that \(AD = 6\), \(DB = 4\), \(AE = 9\), and \(DE\) is parallel to \(BC\). Furthermore, \(DE = 12\). Calculate the length of \(BC\).
question.ar: In the given diagram, \(\triangle ABC\) is inscribed in a circle. Points \(D\) and \(E\) lie on sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) respectively. It is إذا علمت أن \(AD = 6\), \(DB = 4\), \(AE = 9\), and \(DE\) is موازٍ لـ \(BC\). Furthermore, \(DE = 12\). احسب length of \(BC\).

hints.en: Since \(DE \parallel BC\), by the property of similar triangles (Thales's Theorem or Basic Proportionality Theorem), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\).
hints.ar: Since \(DE \parallel BC\), بتطبيق property of similar triangles (Thales's Theorem or Basic Proportionality Theorem), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\).

hints.en: The ratio of corresponding sides in similar triangles is equal. Therefore, we have: \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{AE}{AC} = \frac{DE}{BC}\) We are given \(AD = 6\) and \(DB = 4\). So, \(AB = AD + DB = 6 + 4\).
hints.ar: The ratio of corresponding sides in similar triangles is equal. وبالتالي، we have: \(\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{AE}{AC} = \frac{DE}{BC}\) We are given \(AD = 6\) and \(DB = 4\). So, \(AB = AD + DB = 6 + 4\).

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(6 \times BC\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(6 \times BC\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
Since \(DE \parallel BC\), by the property of similar triangles (Thales's Theorem or Basic Proportionality Theorem), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). 

The ratio of corresponding sides in similar triangles is equal. Therefore, we have:
\[ \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{AE}{AC} = \frac{DE}{BC} \]

We are given \(AD = 6\) and \(DB = 4\). So, \(AB = AD + DB = 6 + 4 = 10\).
We are given \(AE = 9\) and \(DE = 12\).

Using the ratio of similarity:
\[ \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{DE}{BC} \]
Substitute the known values:
\[ \frac{6}{10} = \frac{12}{BC} \]

Now, solve for \(BC\):
\[ 6 \times BC = 10 \times 12 \]
\[ 6 \times BC = 120 \]
\[ BC = \frac{120}{6} \]
\[ BC = 20 \]
